LETTER:
To the Road Authority

We are writing about the crossing outside our school at the Hill View Road site monitored by Crossing Watch.

In a 3.0 minute recording of 180.0 s we counted 8 pedestrian crossings and 10 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 32.2 km/h. Had a child been struck, the impact would almost certainly have been fatal. 3 of 8 crossings (1 in 2.7) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 2 of 8 (1 in 4) within 1.5 s. The exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 8.5-75.5% and 3.2-65.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

We recorded 2 serious near-misses defined as less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart. A serious near-miss had a PET of 1.1 s with a motorcycle at 33.9 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at 33.9 km/h the estimated death risk is 2.1% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
A 2nd serious near-miss had a PET of 0.0 s with a motorcycle at 16.6 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at 16.6 km/h the estimated death risk is 0.4% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
A close pass had a PET of 1.5 s with a car at 24.7 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at 24.7 km/h the estimated death risk is 0.9% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
At a 20 km/h limit the impact speeds would have been 5.9 km/h, 16.6 km/h and 6.5 km/h with adult death risks of 0.2%, 0.4% and 0.2% respectively.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 3.0 minutes. 73.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps, 6 of them 12 s or more and longest 24.5 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to lower speeds and provide protected gaps.

We have the tracking data and can share the video file on request to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

We are writing about the crossing outside our school at the Hill View Road site monitored by Crossing Watch.

In a 3.0 minute recording of 180.0 s we counted 8 pedestrian crossings and 10 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 32.2 km/h. These figures come from a single recording and may differ on other days. 3 of 8 crossings (1 in 2.7) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 2 of 8 (1 in 4) within 1.5 s. The exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 8.5-75.5% and 3.2-65.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

We recorded 2 serious near-misses defined as less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart. A serious near-miss had a PET of 1.1 s with a motorcycle at 33.9 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at 33.9 km/h the estimated death risk is 2.1% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
A 2nd serious near-miss had a PET of 0.0 s with a motorcycle at 16.6 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at 16.6 km/h the estimated death risk is 0.4% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
A close pass had a PET of 1.5 s with a car at 24.7 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at 24.7 km/h the estimated death risk is 0.9% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
At a 20 km/h limit the impact speeds would have been 5.9 km/h, 16.6 km/h and 6.5 km/h with adult death risks of 0.2%, 0.4% and 0.2% respectively.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 3.0 minutes. 73.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps, 6 of them 12 s or more and longest 24.5 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to lower speeds and provide protected gaps.

We have the tracking data and can share the video file on request to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We can share the video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at the Bridge Street crossing

Our school arranged Crossing Watch measurements at the Bridge Street crossing made by SAM tracking with road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time. In 29.3 minutes (1758.0 s) of video, 12 crossings and 29 vehicles were recorded, with an 85th percentile speed of 56.5 km/h. These near-misses happened because drivers ignored the crossing markings.

4 of 12 crossings (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 2 of 12 (1 in 6) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 9.9-65.1% and 2.1-48.4% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 1.1-10.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The 2 serious near-misses included one with a post-encroachment time of 1.0 s with an auto-rickshaw at 52.8 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front is 10.5% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.0 s with an auto-rickshaw at 37.1 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front is 2.8%.
A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.8 s with a car at 25.8 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front is 0.4%.
A further close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s with a motorcycle at 21.5 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front is 0.2%.

For context, PV2 was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 25 pedestrians and 59 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 29.3 minutes of video, but a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice at 1.3x the true count in our drone test.
63.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 7 such gaps, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h approach signs at this crossing.
We have retained the video files from the 29.3 minute recording and can share them on request for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write regarding safety outside our school at Lake View Road crossing.

We measured traffic from video for 2.4 minutes. In that time there were 5 pedestrian crossings and 6 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 50.9 km/h. The people crossing in these events were our students.

For context on engineering assessment, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 2.4. In the period recorded, 61.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed.

We recorded 5 serious near-misses. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart.

One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.0 s with a motorcycle travelling at 45.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 5.5%.
One serious near-miss had a PET of 1.1 s with a car travelling at 38.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 3.1%.
One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.7 s with a car travelling at 34.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.3%.
One serious near-miss had a PET of 1.4 s with a van travelling at 23.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.9%.
One serious near-miss had a PET of 1.0 s with a motorcycle travelling at 16.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4%.

Risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosen and Sander 2009.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and protect pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing on Hill View Road

Our school monitored the Hill View Road crossing for 20.1 minutes (1206.0 s). We counted 14 crossings and 23 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 51.9 km/h. Had a child been struck, the impact would almost certainly have been fatal. There was 1 gap of 6 s or more and 1 gap of 12 s or more, with the longest gap 49.4 s.

In that time there were 3 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s apart). In 2 cases the person was first, in 2 cases the vehicle was first, and in 1 case both were at once.

The worst incidents were as follows. 1 serious near-miss involved a van at 48.4 km/h with 1.0 s between road users; the adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 7.3% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). 1 serious near-miss involved a car at 21.8 km/h with 0.0 s between road users; the adult death risk is 0.7%. 1 serious near-miss involved a bus at 16.2 km/h with 0.9 s between road users; the adult death risk is 0.4%. 1 close pass involved a van at 47.8 km/h with 2.7 s between road users. 1 close pass involved a motorcycle at 26.6 km/h with 2.9 s between road users.

For engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 42 pedestrians and 69 vehicles an hour scaled from 20.1 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour. Also 95.1% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, from 1 such gap, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We can share the video for your review and welcome a site inspection.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about the crossing outside our school on Lantern Road. A video recording made by Crossing Watch over 16.8 minutes counted 19 crossings and 24 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 64.9 mph.

In that time, 4 of 19 crossings had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 2 of those were serious near-misses under 1.5 s.

The most severe was a van at 58.2 km/h passing 1.1 s from a person. If an adult had been hit in that case the estimated death risk from a car front is 15.9% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

Another serious near-miss involved a bus at 17.5 km/h with 0.7 s separation.

For context, PV² was recorded as 0.0 x 10^8, but this is scaled from 16.8 minutes of video while a formal check requires the full peak hour. Also, 65.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and associated signs at this location.

We are happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvements at Cedar Lane crossing

We write concerning the crossing outside our school at Cedar Lane crossing. A video survey of 43.5 minutes (2610.0 s) recorded 22 crossings and 15 vehicles.

In that period, 3 of 22 crossings (1 in 7.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 2 of 22 (1 in 11) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 2.9-34.9% and 1.1-29.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The 85th percentile speed was 51.2 km/h. To sum up, the recording showed 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and close pass as 1.5-3.0 s. There were 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.4 s and involved an auto-rickshaw at 49.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 8.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

A second serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s and involved a bus at 12.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s and involved a car at 25.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, based on 30 pedestrians and 21 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 43.5 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can double-count.

Also, 49.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 gaps, 4 of them 12 s or more, and the longest 84.8 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority
Subject: Request for safer crossing outside school on River Lane

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write regarding the River Lane crossing outside our school. Crossing Watch recorded 25 crossings in 36.0 minutes with 10 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 56.9 km/h. Mrs. Leela Fernandes, who drives the morning bus, caused the worst of these events.

In that period 2 of 25 crossings (1 in 12) were serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 of 25 (1 in 12) were within 3 s. Exact 95% ranges if this recording is typical are 1.0-26.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The most severe was a bus at 52.9 km/h passing 0.1 s after a person. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 10.6% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

The second serious near-miss was a van at 22.9 km/h passing 1.3 s after a person. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.8%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, scaled from 36.0 minutes of video while a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice. Also, 62.4% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 3 such gaps and longest 81.8 s, though the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for pupils crossing.

We have the video and tracking data and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority
Subject: Request for safety improvement at Ring Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school monitored the Ring Road crossing outside the school from video for 20.8 minutes (1248.0 s). In that time we recorded 32 crossings and 21 vehicles. Across 20.8 minutes, 32 crossings were seen while 8 intervals of at least 6 s occurred. The 85th percentile speed was 55.2 km/h.

The analysis found 3 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 close pass (1.5-3.0 s). Of the 4 interactions, 2 were person-first and 2 were vehicle-first.

One serious near-miss had a PET of 1.3 s with a car at 57.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed, the death risk is 15.1% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
Another serious near-miss had a PET of 1.3 s with a car at 36.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed, the death risk is 2.6%.
A third serious near-miss had a PET of 0.8 s with a bus at 14.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed, the death risk is 0.4%.
One close pass had a PET of 2.5 s with a van at 30.2 km/h.

For engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 (92 pedestrians and 61 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 20.8 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice: 1.3x the true count in our drone test). Also, 46.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps in total and 4 of them 12 s or more and longest 86.3 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We can share the video and Crossing Watch measurements (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Brook Street crossing

I write as head of the school beside Brook Street crossing. A video survey by Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measured 7 pedestrian crossings and 34 moving vehicles in 4.9 minutes (294.0 s).

The 85th percentile speed was 59.4 km/h. This is what happens at the crossing on each day of the school week. Regarding gaps, 43.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 11 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 58.4 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video. PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this recording is 4.9 minutes, so those rates are not reported.

We recorded 3 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s). Arrival order was 1 person first, 3 vehicle first and 1 both at once.

The worst cases were:
One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.0 s with an auto-rickshaw at 17.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.
A second serious near-miss had a PET of 1.2 s with an auto-rickshaw at 18.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5%.
A third serious near-miss had a PET of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 13.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.
One close pass had a PET of 1.8 s with a car at 57.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 8.1%.
One close pass had a PET of 2.8 s with a car at 50.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0%.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone with signs at Brook Street crossing.

We are willing to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school – Cedar Lane

We write concerning the crossing outside our school on Cedar Lane. An independent video review (Crossing Watch, SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) observed 24.8 minutes (1488.0 s) at the site and counted 14 crossings and 19 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 59.9 km/h. The counts above are past the threshold the road code sets for a zebra crossing.

The review classified 3 events as serious, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 events as close passes defined as 1.5-3.0 s. In 2 cases the person was first, in 2 cases the vehicle was first, and in 1 case both were at once.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 52.2 km/h with a gap of 0.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 10.0% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, which would fall to 0.2% at an impact of 8.4 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

Another serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 50.2 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s. The report notes an adult death risk of 8.5% if hit at that speed.

A third serious near-miss involved a van at 31.2 km/h with a gap of 0.0 s. The report notes an adult death risk of 1.6% if hit at that speed.

A close pass involved a car at 55.2 km/h with a gap of 2.5 s.

A further close pass involved a car at 33.1 km/h with a gap of 2.1 s.

The engineering note estimates PV² as 0.0 x 10^8 scaled from 24.8 minutes of video, noting that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count one person twice. 95.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, in 4 gaps with the longest 83.9 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this location. We can share the video and measurement details for your review.

Yours faithfully,

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school – Cedar Lane

We write concerning the crossing outside our school on Cedar Lane. An independent video review (Crossing Watch, SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) observed 24.8 minutes (1488.0 s) at the site and counted 14 crossings and 19 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 59.9 km/h.

The review classified three events as serious, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 events as close passes defined as 1.5-3.0 s. In 2 cases the person was first, in 2 cases the vehicle was first, and in 1 case both were at once.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 52.2 km/h with a gap of 0.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 10.0% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, which would fall to 0.2% at an impact of 8.4 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

Another serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 50.2 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s. The report notes an adult death risk of 8.5% if hit at that speed.

A third serious near-miss involved a van at 31.2 km/h with a gap of 0.0 s. The report notes an adult death risk of 1.6% if hit at that speed.

A close pass involved a car at 55.2 km/h with a gap of 2.5 s.

A further close pass involved a car at 33.1 km/h with a gap of 2.1 s.

The engineering note estimates PV² as 0.0 x 10^8 scaled from 24.8 minutes of video, noting that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count one person twice. 95.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, in 4 gaps with the longest 83.9 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this location. We can share the video and measurement details for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school – Cedar Lane

We write concerning the crossing outside our school on Cedar Lane. An independent video review (Crossing Watch, SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) observed 24.8 minutes (1488.0 s) at the site and counted 14 crossings and 19 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 59.9 km/h. The closest of these passes was in fact a collision.

The review classified 3 events as serious, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 events as close passes defined as 1.5-3.0 s. In 2 cases the person was first, in 2 cases the vehicle was first, and in 1 case both were at once.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 52.2 km/h with a gap of 0.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 10.0% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, which would fall to 0.2% at an impact of 8.4 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

Another serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 50.2 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s. The report notes an adult death risk of 8.5% if hit at that speed.

A third serious near-miss involved a van at 31.2 km/h with a gap of 0.0 s. The report notes an adult death risk of 1.6% if hit at that speed.

A close pass involved a car at 55.2 km/h with a gap of 2.5 s.

A further close pass involved a car at 33.1 km/h with a gap of 2.1 s.

The engineering note estimates PV² as 0.0 x 10^8 scaled from 24.8 minutes of video, noting that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count one person twice. 95.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, in 4 gaps with the longest 83.9 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this location. We can share the video and measurement details for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority,

We write concerning the crossing outside our school at Brook Street crossing.

We arranged video monitoring using SAM tracking with road-plane geometry. In 17.4 minutes we recorded 20 pedestrian crossings and 24 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 44.9 km/h. The death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). There were 2 serious near-misses where pedestrian and moving vehicle were on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 4 close passes between 1.5 s and 3.0 s.

The most severe event had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s and involved a motorcycle. That motorcycle was travelling at 37.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 2.8%.

A second serious event had a post-encroachment time of 0.5 s and involved a car. That car was travelling at 17.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 0.5%.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.6 s and involved a bus. That bus was travelling at 22.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 0.6%.

A further close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.8 s and involved a motorcycle. That motorcycle was travelling at 22.8 km/h.

A final close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.5 s and involved a bus. That bus was travelling at 30.8 km/h. All risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009.

Engineering review noted PV² of 0.0 x 10^8 based on 69 pedestrians and 83 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 17.4 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can double-count. It also noted 56.4% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 5 such gaps and longest 11.1 s, though the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a speed table to reduce speeds and provide protected crossing time.

We are happy to share the video and underlying measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about the pedestrian crossing outside our school on River Lane. We arranged a Crossing Watch measurement of the crossing. In 7.0 minutes (420.0 s) it counted 11 pedestrian crossings and 10 moving vehicles, with an 85th-percentile speed of 54.4 km/h. With this measure in place there will be no more fatalities here. There were 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes, defined as 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart. Where order could be seen, 4 interactions were person-first and 1 was vehicle-first.

The most severe near-miss was 0.3 s apart with a car at 49.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled adult death risk is 7.9%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second serious near-miss was 1.2 s apart with a bus at 48.7 km/h, with a modelled adult death risk of 7.5% if hit.

A third serious near-miss was 1.2 s apart with a car at 45.7 km/h, with a modelled adult death risk of 5.8% if hit.

On engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 7.0, so results are indicative only. 48.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 gaps, 0 of them 12 s or more, and the longest 8.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce approach speeds and give pedestrians clear priority.

We can share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review and would welcome a site visit to discuss the design.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by The Principal as head of the school

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Ring Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

I write on behalf of the school located at the Ring Road crossing to request a safety improvement.

We commissioned a video review of the crossing. During 4.0 minutes (240.0 s) of video, 3 pedestrian crossings and 13 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 49.5 km/h. Among the worst near-misses measured, the fastest vehicle was going at 45.4 km/h.

No serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) were recorded. There were 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s apart).

The first close pass involved a van at 16.8 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s.

The second close pass involved a bus at 45.4 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.7 s.

For adults hit by a car front, Rosén & Sander 2009 estimates the adult death risk if hit in these incidents would have been 0.0% for the van and 0.0% for the bus, and 0.0% at a 20 km/h limit.

The engineering note advises that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this video is 4.0 minutes.

In this video 63.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps of 6 s or more and 6 of 12 s or more, the longest 81.9 s. The note states the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds, while other groups such as children may need 10-12 s or longer.

We therefore request installation of a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements to support your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Safety of the pedestrian crossing on Cedar Lane

We write to request a raised zebra crossing outside our school.

Crossing Watch measurements over 4.7 minutes recorded 12 pedestrian crossings and 19 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 54.8 km/h. One near-miss ended with the vehicle hitting the person crossing.

2 serious near-misses and 4 close passes were recorded. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. Close pass is defined as 1.5 to 3.0 s apart.

One serious near-miss involved a bus at 40.3 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 3.7%.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 35.1 km/h with a gap of 0.2 s. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 2.3%.

One close pass involved an auto-rickshaw at 50.2 km/h with a gap of 1.8 s.

One close pass involved a car at 34.6 km/h with a gap of 1.9 s.

One close pass involved a van at 21.9 km/h with a gap of 2.4 s.

All death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosen and Sander 2009.

Engineering context with caveats: PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 4.7 minutes. 61.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 7 gaps, 7 of them 12 s or more, longest 19.4 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We therefore request that you provide a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and protect children and adults crossing.

We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review and would welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write to request a safety improvement at the crossing outside our school. We commissioned a Crossing Watch measurement using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry to assess post-encroachment time.

Over 11.1 minutes (666.0 s) the video counted twelve pedestrian crossings and 11 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 48.4 km/h. In that period 4 of 12 crossings (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 3 of 12 crossings (1 in 4) were within 1.5 s.
Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 9.9-65.1% and 5.5-57.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The video found 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart. The worst serious near-miss was 1.2 s apart involving an auto-rickshaw at 47.4 km/h. A second serious near-miss was 0.2 s apart involving a van at 44.0 km/h. A third serious near-miss was 0.4 s apart involving an auto-rickshaw at 13.1 km/h. The close pass was 1.9 s apart involving a car at 50.1 km/h.
For adults hit by a car front, Rosén and Sander 2009 gives an adult death risk if hit of 6.7% for the 47.4 km/h case, 5.0% for the 44.0 km/h case, 0.3% for the 13.1 km/h case, and 3.2% for the 50.1 km/h case. At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speed would be 0.0 km/h with 0.0% adult death risk for the 47.4 km/h case, 20.0 km/h with 0.6% adult death risk for the 44.0 km/h case, 13.1 km/h with 0.3% adult death risk for the 13.1 km/h case, and 0.0 km/h with 0.0% adult death risk for the 50.1 km/h case.

For context, PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 11.1 minutes. The recording also shows 66.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 such gaps and 3 of them 12 s or more and a longest gap of 33.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h markings at this location.

We are willing to share the video and measurement files for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by The Principal on behalf of the School Management Committee

LETTER:
To the Road Authority,

We write concerning the crossing outside our school at Brook Street crossing.

We arranged video monitoring using SAM tracking with road-plane geometry. In 17.4 minutes we recorded 20 pedestrian crossings and 24 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 44.9 km/h. The closest of these near-misses was the fault of Mr. Tarun Mehra, who runs the tea stall. There were 2 serious near-misses where pedestrian and moving vehicle were on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 4 close passes between 1.5 s and 3.0 s.

The most severe event had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s and involved a motorcycle. That motorcycle was travelling at 37.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 2.8%.

A second serious event had a post-encroachment time of 0.5 s and involved a car. That car was travelling at 17.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 0.5%.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.6 s and involved a bus. That bus was travelling at 22.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 0.6%.

A further close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.8 s and involved a motorcycle. That motorcycle was travelling at 22.8 km/h.

A final close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.5 s and involved a bus. That bus was travelling at 30.8 km/h. All risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009.

Engineering review noted PV² of 0.0 x 10^8 based on 69 pedestrians and 83 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 17.4 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can double-count. It also noted 56.4% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 5 such gaps and longest 11.1 s, though the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a speed table to reduce speeds and provide protected crossing time.

We are happy to share the video and underlying measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at River Lane crossing

Dear Sir or Madam,

On behalf of the school beside River Lane crossing, I write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone with signs. The recording these figures come from lasted 6.8 minutes.

Crossing Watch video observation lasted 6.8 minutes (408.0 s). During that time 4 pedestrian crossings and 32 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 39.7 km/h.

In that period there were 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass defined as 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. In 3 cases the pedestrian was first and in 1 case the vehicle was first.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 41.4 km/h with a separation of 0.8 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 4.0 percent, based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15 plus. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 15.5 km/h with a death risk of 0.4 percent.

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 20.6 km/h with a separation of 1.0 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.6 percent. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6 percent.

A third serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 12.9 km/h with a separation of 0.3 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3 percent. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 12.9 km/h with a death risk of 0.3 percent.

One close pass involved a car at 16.0 km/h with a separation of 2.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0 percent.

Regarding longer-term warrants, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 6.8. The share of time inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed was 95.7 percent, from 8 gaps of 6 s or more including 2 gaps of 12 s or more with the longest gap 83.4 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. For reference, the UK Traffic Signs Manual chapter 6, 13.5.2 notes that 4 to 6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups such as children may need 10 to 12 s or longer.

We request the raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone as a physical fix to lower speeds and create safe gaps. We are willing to share the full video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 20.6 km/h with a separation of 1.0 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.6 percent. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6 percent.

One close pass involved a car at 16.0 km/h with a separation of 2.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0 percent.

Regarding longer-term warrants, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 6.8. The share of time inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed was 95.7 percent, from 8 gaps of 6 s or more including 2 gaps of 12 s or more with the longest gap 83.4 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. We request the raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone as a physical fix to lower speeds and create safe gaps. We are willing to share the full video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside the school on Lake View Road

We write regarding the crossing outside our school on Lake View Road. A Crossing Watch review of 21.4 minutes of video (1284.0 s) recorded 11 crossings and 22 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 50.9 km/h. A young pupil hit by the fastest vehicle would probably not have survived.

The review found 4 of 11 crossings (1 in 2.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 3 of 11 (1 in 3.7) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 10.9-69.2% and 6.0-61.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 3 serious near-misses and 1 close pass as defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1.5-3.0 s respectively.

The worst near-misses were:
One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with a car at 51.3 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 9.2% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 42.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 4.5%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s with an auto-rickshaw at 37.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 2.9%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s with a car at 51.5 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 6.1%.

In engineering terms, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 31 pedestrians and 62 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 21.4 minutes of video, and a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice as 1.3x the true count in our drone test. Also 43.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 gaps and 1 of them 12 s or more and longest 17.6 s, with the caveat that the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We write regarding the crossing outside our school on Lake View Road. A Crossing Watch review of 21.4 minutes of video (1284.0 s) recorded 11 crossings and 22 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 50.9 km/h. Near-misses like these occur every morning when school opens.

There were 3 serious near-misses and 1 close pass as defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1.5-3.0 s respectively.

The worst near-misses were:
One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with a car at 51.3 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 9.2% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 42.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 4.5%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s with a car at 51.5 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 6.1%.

In engineering terms, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 31 pedestrians and 62 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 21.4 minutes of video, and a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice as 1.3x the true count in our drone test. Also 43.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 gaps and 1 of them 12 s or more and longest 17.6 s, with the caveat that the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We write regarding the crossing outside our school on Lake View Road. A Crossing Watch review of 21.4 minutes of video (1284.0 s) recorded 11 crossings and 22 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 50.9 km/h. Many of these drivers were not watching the road at all.

There were 3 serious near-misses and 1 close pass as defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1.5-3.0 s respectively.

The worst near-misses were:
One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with a car at 51.3 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 9.2% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 42.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 4.5%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s with an auto-rickshaw at 37.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 2.9%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s with a car at 51.5 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 6.1%.

In engineering terms, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 31 pedestrians and 62 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 21.4 minutes of video, and a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice as 1.3x the true count in our drone test. Yours faithfully,

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write regarding the crossing on School Lane outside our school.

We measured traffic for 11.9 minutes and counted 7 pedestrian crossings and 40 moving vehicles.

The 85th percentile speed was 42.3 km/h. Had a child been struck, the impact would almost certainly have been fatal.

We recorded 3 serious near-misses and 3 close passes.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 34.8 km/h with 0.7 s between road users, with a 2.3% adult death risk if hit by a car front, which would fall to 0.6% adult death risk at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

Another serious near-miss involved a van at 27.0 km/h with 0.4 s between road users, with a 1.1% adult death risk if hit by a car front, which would fall to 0.6% adult death risk at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

A third serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 24.4 km/h with 1.3 s between road users, with a 0.9% adult death risk if hit by a car front, which would fall to 0.5% adult death risk at an impact of 17.7 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 11.9 minutes.

Only 40.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to reduce speeds and provide a safe crossing point.

We are willing to share the video of the crossing for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write regarding Quarry Road crossing outside our school.

In 38.2 minutes of video we recorded 9 crossings and 4 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 64.0 km/h. All of the pedestrians involved were children on their way home. There were 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 0 close passes of 1.5 to 3.0 s.

The calculated PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 14 pedestrians and 6 vehicles per hour scaled from 38.2 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can overcount by 1.3x in our drone test. 90.2% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 6 gaps, 1 of them 12 s or more, longest 77.8 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

One serious near-miss involved a van at 56.1 km/h with 0.6 s between pedestrian and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 13.5% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, and at a 20 km/h limit the impact would have been 14.7 km/h with 0.4% risk.

Another serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 52.9 km/h with 1.1 s between pedestrian and vehicle. For an adult hit at that speed the death risk is 10.5%, and at a 20 km/h limit the impact would have been 0.0 km/h with 0.0% risk.

A third serious near-miss involved a car at 37.5 km/h with 0.0 s between pedestrian and vehicle. For an adult hit at that speed the death risk is 2.9%, and at a 20 km/h limit the impact would have been 20.0 km/h with 0.6% risk.

We request you provide a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing point.

We can share the 38.2 minutes of video and tracking data on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write regarding the crossing on School Lane outside our school.

We measured traffic for 11.9 minutes and counted 7 pedestrian crossings and 40 moving vehicles.

The 85th percentile speed was 42.3 km/h.

We recorded 3 serious near-misses and 3 close passes.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 34.8 km/h with 0.7 s between road users, with a 2.3% adult death risk if hit by a car front, which would fall to 0.6% adult death risk at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

Another serious near-miss involved a van at 27.0 km/h with 0.4 s between road users, with a 1.1% adult death risk if hit by a car front, which would fall to 0.6% adult death risk at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

A third serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 24.4 km/h with 1.3 s between road users, with a 0.9% adult death risk if hit by a car front, which would fall to 0.5% adult death risk at an impact of 17.7 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 11.9 minutes.

Only 40.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to reduce speeds and provide a safe crossing point.

We are willing to share the video of the crossing for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write regarding the crossing on School Lane outside our school.

We measured traffic for 11.9 minutes and counted 7 pedestrian crossings and 40 moving vehicles.

The 85th percentile speed was 42.3 km/h. The death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

We recorded 3 serious near-misses and 3 close passes.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 34.8 km/h with 0.7 s between road users, with a 2.3% adult death risk if hit by a car front, which would fall to 0.6% adult death risk at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

Another serious near-miss involved a van at 27.0 km/h with 0.4 s between road users, with a 1.1% adult death risk if hit by a car front, which would fall to 0.6% adult death risk at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

A third serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 24.4 km/h with 1.3 s between road users, with a 0.9% adult death risk if hit by a car front, which would fall to 0.5% adult death risk at an impact of 17.7 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 11.9 minutes.

Only 40.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to reduce speeds and provide a safe crossing point.

We are willing to share the video of the crossing for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We are happy to share the video and measurements to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school on Park Avenue

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school monitored the crossing outside it for 38.4 minutes (2304.0 s). In that time we recorded 32 crossings and 17 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 26.3 km/h. The people crossing in these events were our students. We observed 1 serious near-miss and 2 close passes.

By definition, a serious near-miss is when a pedestrian and a moving vehicle are on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and a close pass is 1.5 to 3.0 s apart.

The serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.4 s and involved a car at 14.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at 14.2 km/h the death risk from Rosén & Sander 2009 is 0.4%.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.1 s and involved a van at 13.8 km/h.

A further close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.4 s and involved a car at 24.6 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 50 pedestrians and 27 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 38.4 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count one person twice, by 1.3x in our drone test. 

Also, 67.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps and 7 of them 12 s or more and longest gap 33.8 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you provide a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this crossing to reduce vehicle speeds and to give pedestrians priority.

We are happy to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,

The Principal

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school on Park Avenue

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school monitored the crossing outside it for 38.4 minutes (2304.0 s). In that time we recorded 32 crossings and 17 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 26.3 km/h. The recording these figures come from lasted 38.4 minutes. We observed 1 serious near-miss and 2 close passes.

By definition, a serious near-miss is when a pedestrian and a moving vehicle are on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and a close pass is 1.5 to 3.0 s apart.

The serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.4 s and involved a car at 14.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at 14.2 km/h the death risk from Rosén & Sander 2009 is 0.4%.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.1 s and involved a van at 13.8 km/h.

A further close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.4 s and involved a car at 24.6 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 50 pedestrians and 27 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 38.4 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count one person twice, by 1.3x in our drone test. 

Also, 67.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps and 7 of them 12 s or more and longest gap 33.8 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you provide a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this crossing to reduce vehicle speeds and to give pedestrians priority.

We are happy to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,

The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside the school

We write to request a raised zebra crossing with 20 km/h zone, signs and markings outside our school. The closest of these near-misses was the fault of Mr. Tarun Mehra, who runs the tea stall. A supervised video measurement of 6.8 minutes recorded 5 pedestrian crossings and 38 moving vehicles with an 85th percentile speed of 53.1 km/h.

Of 5 crossings, 5 had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s and 3 were within 1.5 s. If this recording is typical, the exact 95 percent ranges are 47.8-100.0 percent and 14.7-94.7 percent of crossings and 1.6-11.7 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long.

The worst near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 48.3 km/h with a gap of 0.0 s. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is given as 7.2 percent, compared with 0.6 percent at 20.0 km/h. 
A second serious near-miss involved a car at 17.5 km/h with a gap of 0.0 s. 
A third serious near-miss involved a van at 12.9 km/h with a gap of 0.4 s.

Engineering values are limited: PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 6.8 minutes, and 43.2 percent of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request the fix above to reduce speeds and protect children crossing. We are willing to share the video and measurement file for verification.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvements at Cedar Lane crossing

We write concerning the crossing outside our school at Cedar Lane crossing. A video survey of 43.5 minutes (2610.0 s) recorded 22 crossings and 15 vehicles. Many of those crossing were young pupils hurrying to school.

In that period, 3 of 22 crossings (1 in 7.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 2 of 22 (1 in 11) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 2.9-34.9% and 1.1-29.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The 85th percentile speed was 51.2 km/h. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and close pass as 1.5-3.0 s. There were 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.4 s and involved an auto-rickshaw at 49.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 8.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

A second serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s and involved a bus at 12.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s and involved a car at 25.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, based on 30 pedestrians and 21 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 43.5 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can double-count.

Also, 49.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 gaps, 4 of them 12 s or more, and the longest 84.8 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Subject: Request for safety improvement at River Lane crossing

Dear Sir or Madam,

On behalf of the school beside River Lane crossing, I write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone with signs. We would be glad to walk the crossing with your engineers whenever it suits them.

Crossing Watch video observation lasted 6.8 minutes (408.0 s). During that time 4 pedestrian crossings and 32 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 39.7 km/h.

In that period there were 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass defined as 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. In 3 cases the pedestrian was first and in 1 case the vehicle was first.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 41.4 km/h with a separation of 0.8 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 4.0 percent, based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15 plus. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 15.5 km/h with a death risk of 0.4 percent.

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 20.6 km/h with a separation of 1.0 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.6 percent. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6 percent.

A third serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 12.9 km/h with a separation of 0.3 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3 percent. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 12.9 km/h with a death risk of 0.3 percent.

One close pass involved a car at 16.0 km/h with a separation of 2.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0 percent.

Regarding longer-term warrants, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 6.8. The share of time inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed was 95.7 percent, from 8 gaps of 6 s or more including 2 gaps of 12 s or more with the longest gap 83.4 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. For reference, the UK Traffic Signs Manual chapter 6, 13.5.2 notes that 4 to 6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups such as children may need 10 to 12 s or longer.

We request the raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone as a physical fix to lower speeds and create safe gaps. We are willing to share the full video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at River Lane crossing

Dear Sir or Madam,

On behalf of the school beside River Lane crossing, I write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 mph zone with signs.

Crossing Watch video observation lasted 6.8 minutes (408.0 s). During that time 4 pedestrian crossings and 32 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 39.7 km/h.

In that period there were 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass defined as 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. In 3 cases the pedestrian was first and in 1 case the vehicle was first.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 41.4 km/h with a separation of 0.8 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 4.0 percent, based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15 plus. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 15.5 km/h with a death risk of 0.4 percent.

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 20.6 km/h with a separation of 1.0 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.6 percent. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6 percent.

A third serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 12.9 km/h with a separation of 0.3 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3 percent. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 12.9 km/h with a death risk of 0.3 percent.

One close pass involved a car at 16.0 km/h with a separation of 2.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0 percent.

Regarding longer-term warrants, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 6.8. The share of time inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed was 95.7 percent, from 8 gaps of 6 s or more including 2 gaps of 12 s or more with the longest gap 83.4 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the Cedar Lane crossing outside our school. Crossing Watch tracking using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry over 31.5 minutes recorded 29 crossings and 28 vehicles, with an 85th-percentile speed of 48.0 mph.

In that time 5 of 29 crossings (1 in 5.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person, and 1 of 29 (1 in 29) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges if this recording is typical are 5.8-35.8% and 0.1-17.8% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.6-11.7 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The worst events were post-encroachment time measured as serious below 1.5 s and close pass 1.5-3.0 s. A serious near-miss had a gap of 1.1 s as a car passed at 42.2 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit by a car front of 4.3%.
A close pass had a gap of 1.5 s as a car passed at 44.4 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 5.2%.
A close pass had a gap of 1.9 s as a van passed at 35.5 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.8%.
A close pass had a gap of 2.5 s as a motorcycle passed at 38.5 km/h.
A close pass had a gap of 2.8 s as a car passed at 33.6 km/h.
All death-risk figures are Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts at 20 km/h limit the impact would be 0.0 km/h with 0.0% risk in these cases.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 for 55 pedestrians and 53 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 31.5 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour. 55.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 3 gaps, 0 of them 12 s or more, longest 10.0 s, where the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to reduce approach speeds and give priority to pupils crossing. We are happy to share the video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Ring Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

I write on behalf of the school located at the Ring Road crossing to request a safety improvement.

We commissioned a video review of the crossing. During 4.0 minutes (240.0 s) of video, 3 pedestrian crossings and 13 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 49.5 km/h. There have already been injuries at this spot this school year.

No serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) were recorded. There were 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s apart).

The first close pass involved a van at 16.8 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s.

The second close pass involved a bus at 45.4 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.7 s.

For adults hit by a car front, Rosén & Sander 2009 estimates the adult death risk if hit in these incidents would have been 0.0% for the van and 0.0% for the bus, and 0.0% at a 20 km/h limit.

The engineering note advises that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this video is 4.0 minutes.

In this video 63.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps of 6 s or more and 6 of 12 s or more, the longest 81.9 s. The note states the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds, while other groups such as children may need 10-12 s or longer.

We therefore request installation of a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements to support your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Brook Street crossing

I write as head of the school beside Brook Street crossing. A video survey by Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measured 7 pedestrian crossings and 34 moving vehicles in 4.9 minutes (294.0 s).

The 85th percentile speed was 59.4 km/h. Regarding gaps, 43.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 11 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 58.4 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video. PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this recording is 4.9 minutes, so those rates are not reported.

We recorded 3 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s). Arrival order was 1 person first, 3 vehicle first and 1 both at once. During 294.0 s, 7 crossings interacted with 34 vehicles, producing 3 serious near-misses and 2 close passes.

The worst cases were:
One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.0 s with an auto-rickshaw at 17.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.
A second serious near-miss had a PET of 1.2 s with an auto-rickshaw at 18.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5%.
A third serious near-miss had a PET of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 13.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.
One close pass had a PET of 1.8 s with a car at 57.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 8.1%.
One close pass had a PET of 2.8 s with a car at 50.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0%.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone with signs at Brook Street crossing.

We are willing to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school on Station Road

We write following a Crossing Watch measurement at the Station Road crossing over 24.2 minutes (1452.0 s). In that time 38 crossings and 8 vehicles were recorded, the 85th percentile speed was 44.1 km/h, there were 8 gaps of 6 s or more and 7 gaps of 12 s or more with the longest gap 53.4 s, and 89.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more. One near-miss ended with the vehicle hitting the person crossing. 6 of 38 crossings (1 in 6.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 5 of 38 (1 in 7.6) within 1.5 s; exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 6.0-31.3% and 4.4-28.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 1.6-11.7 people in a recording this long (Poisson). Of the 6 events within 3 s, 4 were person first and 2 were vehicle first, with 5 serious near-misses less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass 1.5-3.0 s apart as defined.

The 5 serious near-misses were as follows. One involved a bus at 44.5 km/h with 1.0 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 5.2% death risk (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved a car at 39.5 km/h with 1.2 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 3.4% death risk, compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved an auto-rickshaw at 37.6 km/h with 0.3 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 2.9% death risk, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved an auto-rickshaw at 27.9 km/h with 0.7 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 1.2% death risk, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved a car at 21.4 km/h with 0.5 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 0.7% death risk, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h.

The engineering note recorded PV² as 0.0 x 10^8 from 94 pedestrians and 20 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 24.2 minutes, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice (1.3x in our drone test). It also recorded that 89.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this location to slow traffic to 20 km/h and protect those crossing. We will share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements on request and welcome a site visit.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school on Station Road

We write following a Crossing Watch measurement at the Station Road crossing over 24.2 minutes (1452.0 s). In that time 38 crossings and 8 vehicles were recorded, the 85th percentile speed was 44.1 km/h, there were 8 gaps of 6 s or more and 7 gaps of 12 s or more with the longest gap 53.4 s, and 89.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more. A young pupil hit by the fastest vehicle would probably not have survived. 6 of 38 crossings (1 in 6.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 5 of 38 (1 in 7.6) within 1.5 s; exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 6.0-31.3% and 4.4-28.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 1.6-11.7 people in a recording this long (Poisson). Of the 6 events within 3 s, 4 were person first and 2 were vehicle first, with 5 serious near-misses less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass 1.5-3.0 s apart as defined.

The 5 serious near-misses were as follows. One involved a bus at 44.5 km/h with 1.0 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 5.2% death risk (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved a car at 39.5 km/h with 1.2 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 3.4% death risk, compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved an auto-rickshaw at 37.6 km/h with 0.3 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 2.9% death risk, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved an auto-rickshaw at 27.9 km/h with 0.7 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 1.2% death risk, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved a car at 21.4 km/h with 0.5 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 0.7% death risk, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h.

The engineering note recorded PV² as 0.0 x 10^8 from 94 pedestrians and 20 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 24.2 minutes, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice (1.3x in our drone test). It also recorded that 89.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this location to slow traffic to 20 km/h and protect those crossing. We will share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements on request and welcome a site visit.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school on Station Road

We write following a Crossing Watch measurement at the Station Road crossing over 24.2 minutes (1452.0 s). In that time 38 crossings and 8 vehicles were recorded, the 85th percentile speed was 44.1 km/h, there were 8 gaps of 6 s or more and 7 gaps of 12 s or more with the longest gap 53.4 s, and 89.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more. 6 of 38 crossings (1 in 6.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 5 of 38 (1 in 7.6) within 1.5 s; exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 6.0-31.3% and 4.4-28.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 1.6-11.7 people in a recording this long (Poisson). Of the 6 events within 3 s, 4 were person first and 2 were vehicle first, with 5 serious near-misses less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass 1.5-3.0 s apart as defined.

The 5 serious near-misses were as follows. One involved a bus at 44.5 km/h with 1.0 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 5.2% death risk (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved a car at 39.5 km/h with 1.2 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 3.4% death risk, compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved an auto-rickshaw at 37.6 km/h with 0.3 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 2.9% death risk, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved an auto-rickshaw at 27.9 km/h with 0.7 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 1.2% death risk, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved a car at 21.4 km/h with 0.5 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 0.7% death risk, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h.

The engineering note recorded PV² as 0.0 x 10^8 from 94 pedestrians and 20 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 24.2 minutes, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice (1.3x in our drone test). It also recorded that 89.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this location to slow traffic to 20 km/h and protect those crossing. We will share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements on request and welcome a site visit.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority
Subject: Request for safety improvement at Ring Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school monitored the Ring Road crossing outside the school from video for 20.8 minutes (1248.0 s). In that time we recorded 32 crossings and 21 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 55.2 km/h. In the near-miss with a time gap of 1.3 s the vehicle was going at 57.5 km/h, and in the one with a time gap of 0.8 s it was going at 14.8 km/h.

The analysis found 3 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 close pass (1.5-3.0 s). Of the 4 interactions, 2 were person-first and 2 were vehicle-first.

One serious near-miss had a PET of 1.3 s with a car at 57.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed, the death risk is 15.1% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
Another serious near-miss had a PET of 1.3 s with a car at 36.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed, the death risk is 2.6%.
A third serious near-miss had a PET of 0.8 s with a bus at 14.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed, the death risk is 0.4%.
One close pass had a PET of 2.5 s with a van at 30.2 km/h.

For engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 (92 pedestrians and 61 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 20.8 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice: 1.3x the true count in our drone test). Also, 46.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps in total and 4 of them 12 s or more and longest 86.3 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We can share the video and Crossing Watch measurements (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
