LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at River Lane crossing

Dear Sir or Madam,

On behalf of the school beside River Lane crossing, I write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone with signs. Had a child been struck, the impact would almost certainly have been fatal.

Crossing Watch video observation lasted 6.8 minutes (408.0 s). During that time 4 pedestrian crossings and 32 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 39.7 km/h.

In that period there were 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass defined as 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. In 3 cases the pedestrian was first and in 1 case the vehicle was first.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 41.4 km/h with a separation of 0.8 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 4.0 percent, based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15 plus. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 15.5 km/h with a death risk of 0.4 percent.

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 20.6 km/h with a separation of 1.0 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.6 percent. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6 percent.

A third serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 12.9 km/h with a separation of 0.3 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3 percent. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 12.9 km/h with a death risk of 0.3 percent.

One close pass involved a car at 16.0 km/h with a separation of 2.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0 percent.

Regarding longer-term warrants, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 6.8. The share of time inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed was 95.7 percent, from 8 gaps of 6 s or more including 2 gaps of 12 s or more with the longest gap 83.4 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. For reference, the UK Traffic Signs Manual chapter 6, 13.5.2 notes that 4 to 6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups such as children may need 10 to 12 s or longer.

We request the raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone as a physical fix to lower speeds and create safe gaps. We are willing to share the full video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

We write concerning the crossing on Garden Road outside our school.

In 17.7 minutes of video we recorded 14 crossings and 6 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 62.3 km/h. The closest of these passes was in fact a collision. Of the 14 crossings, 2 of 14 (1 in 7) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 1 of 14 (1 in 14) within 1.5 s. If this recording is typical the exact 95% ranges are 1.8-42.8% and 0.2-33.9% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.2-7.2 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The most serious near-miss had a gap of 0.6 s between the person and a car; the car was travelling at 56.5 km/h, which carries an adult death risk of 14.0% if hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+). At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed in that event would have been 14.3 km/h with an adult death risk of 0.4%. A second close pass had a gap of 2.6 s with a motorcycle at 17.5 km/h.

On engineering measures, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 for 47 pedestrians and 20 vehicles per hour, but this is scaled from only 17.7 minutes and broken tracks can count one person twice (1.3x in our drone test). Also 68.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps and 7 of 12 s or more and the longest 84.3 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you provide a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this crossing. We would be happy to share the video and the measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Ring Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

I write on behalf of the school located at the Ring Road crossing to request a safety improvement.

We commissioned a video review of the crossing. During 4.0 minutes (240.0 s) of video, 3 pedestrian crossings and 13 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 49.5 km/h. Parents see the same danger here at each school dismissal.

No serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) were recorded. There were 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s apart).

The first close pass involved a van at 16.8 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s.

The second close pass involved a bus at 45.4 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.7 s.

For adults hit by a car front, Rosén & Sander 2009 estimates the adult death risk if hit in these incidents would have been 0.0% for the van and 0.0% for the bus, and 0.0% at a 20 km/h limit.

The engineering note advises that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this video is 4.0 minutes.

In this video 63.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps of 6 s or more and 6 of 12 s or more, the longest 81.9 s. The note states the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds, while other groups such as children may need 10-12 s or longer.

We therefore request installation of a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements to support your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

We write concerning the crossing on Garden Road outside our school.

In 17.7 minutes of video we recorded 14 crossings and 6 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 62.3 km/h. The recording these figures come from lasted 17.7 minutes. Of the 14 crossings, 2 of 14 (1 in 7) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 1 of 14 (1 in 14) within 1.5 s. If this recording is typical the exact 95% ranges are 1.8-42.8% and 0.2-33.9% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.2-7.2 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The most serious near-miss had a gap of 0.6 s between the person and a car; the car was travelling at 56.5 km/h, which carries an adult death risk of 14.0% if hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+). At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed in that event would have been 14.3 km/h with an adult death risk of 0.4%. A second close pass had a gap of 2.6 s with a motorcycle at 17.5 km/h.

On engineering measures, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 for 47 pedestrians and 20 vehicles per hour, but this is scaled from only 17.7 minutes and broken tracks can count one person twice (1.3x in our drone test). Also 68.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps and 7 of 12 s or more and the longest 84.3 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you provide a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this crossing. We would be happy to share the video and the measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Road Authority,

We are writing about safety at the River Lane crossing.

We arranged a Crossing Watch count lasting 7.6 minutes (456.0 s). In that time we counted 3 pedestrian crossings and 1 moving vehicles. Of the crossings, 1 of 3 (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 1 of 3 (1 in 3) within 1.5 s. The 85th percentile speed was 50.4 km/h. This change is certain to save lives at this crossing.

For engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 7.6. Also 81.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 6 gaps of 6 s or more and 5 of 12 s or more, longest 54.5 s, noting the first and last are cut short by the video.

We recorded 1 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 0 close passes (1.5 to 3.0 s).

The worst case was a serious event involving a van travelling at 46.6 km/h. The time gap between road users at the conflict point was 0.2 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 6.2% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6%.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a speed table to reduce speeds and provide protected priority for people crossing.


Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write regarding the crossing outside our school on Lantern Road. We had 41.9 minutes of video reviewed by Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time). In that time 22 people crossed and 29 vehicles passed, with an 85th percentile speed of 51.8 km/h. The counts above are past the threshold the road code sets for a zebra crossing.

The review found 3 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 3 close passes (1.5-3.0 s), with person first in 2 cases and vehicle first in 4 cases.

A serious near-miss with a gap of 1.4 s involving a car at 44.5 km/h, carrying an adult death risk if hit of 5.2%.
A serious near-miss with a gap of 1.1 s involving a car at 44.2 km/h, carrying an adult death risk if hit of 5.1%.
A close pass with a gap of 1.9 s involving a van at 22.6 km/h, carrying an adult death risk if hit of 0.2%.
A close pass with a gap of 2.2 s involving an auto-rickshaw at 28.1 km/h.
All death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009.

For engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 for 32 pedestrians and 42 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 41.9 minutes of video while a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice. 81.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 6 gaps of 6 s or more and 2 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 75.2 s, with first and last gaps cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this crossing to lower speeds and provide a protected crossing point.

We have the video and tracking data and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Ring Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

I write on behalf of the school located at the Ring Road crossing to request a safety improvement.

We commissioned a video review of the crossing. During 4.0 minutes (240.0 s) of video, 3 pedestrian crossings and 13 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 49.5 km/h. The death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

No serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) were recorded. There were 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s apart).

The first close pass involved a van at 16.8 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s.

The second close pass involved a bus at 45.4 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.7 s.

For adults hit by a car front, Rosén & Sander 2009 estimates the adult death risk if hit in these incidents would have been 0.0% for the van and 0.0% for the bus, and 0.0% at a 20 km/h limit.

The engineering note advises that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this video is 4.0 minutes.

In this video 63.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps of 6 s or more and 6 of 12 s or more, the longest 81.9 s. The note states the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds, while other groups such as children may need 10-12 s or longer.

We therefore request installation of a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements to support your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by The Principal

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce speeds and provide priority for people crossing.

We would be pleased to share the video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

During a video observation lasting 2.9 minutes (174.0 s) we counted 9 pedestrian crossings and 24 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 40.4 km/h. By these figures the crossing already qualifies for a signal-controlled crossing.

Yours faithfully,

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Brook Street crossing

I write as head of the school beside Brook Street crossing. A video survey by Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measured seven pedestrian crossings and 34 moving vehicles in 4.9 minutes (294.0 s).

The 85th percentile speed was 59.4 km/h. Regarding gaps, 43.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 11 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 58.4 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video. PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this recording is 4.9 minutes, so those rates are not reported.

We recorded 3 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s). Arrival order was 1 person first, 3 vehicle first and 1 both at once.

The worst cases were:
One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.0 s with an auto-rickshaw at 17.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.
A second serious near-miss had a PET of 1.2 s with an auto-rickshaw at 18.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5%.
A third serious near-miss had a PET of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 13.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.
One close pass had a PET of 1.8 s with a car at 57.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 8.1%.
One close pass had a PET of 2.8 s with a car at 50.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0%.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone with signs at Brook Street crossing.

We are willing to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside school on Hill View Road

We measured traffic at the crossing on Hill View Road for 39.3 minutes. In that time we observed 34 crossings and 21 vehicles. The 85th-percentile speed was 60.0 km/h. The recording these figures come from lasted 39.3 minutes.

We recorded 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes of 1.5 s to 3.0 s. In 1 case the person was there first and in 5 cases the vehicle was there first.

The most severe near-miss involved a car at 56.6 km/h with a gap of 0.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 14.1% based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults aged 15 and above.
Another serious near-miss involved a car at 28.6 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s. The estimated adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.3%.
A further serious near-miss involved a bus at 26.0 km/h with a gap of 0.1 s.
A fourth serious near-miss involved a car at 25.1 km/h with a gap of 0.6 s. The estimated adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.0%.

Engineering indicators were calculated as follows. PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 52 pedestrians and 32 vehicles per hour scaled from the video, noting that a formal check requires the full peak hour and that broken tracks can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x in drone tests. 45.3% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for children crossing. We are willing to share the video and measurement file for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority
Subject: Request for safety improvement at Ring Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school monitored the Ring Road crossing outside the school from video for 20.8 minutes (1248.0 s). In that time we recorded 32 crossings and 21 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 55.2 km/h. We would be glad to walk the crossing with your engineers whenever it suits them.

The analysis found 3 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 close pass (1.5-3.0 s). Of the 4 interactions, 2 were person-first and 2 were vehicle-first.

One serious near-miss had a PET of 1.3 s with a car at 57.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed, the death risk is 15.1% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
Another serious near-miss had a PET of 1.3 s with a car at 36.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed, the death risk is 2.6%.
A third serious near-miss had a PET of 0.8 s with a bus at 14.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed, the death risk is 0.4%.
One close pass had a PET of 2.5 s with a van at 30.2 km/h.

For engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 (92 pedestrians and 61 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 20.8 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice: 1.3x the true count in our drone test). Also, 46.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps in total and 4 of them 12 s or more and longest 86.3 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We can share the video and Crossing Watch measurements (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at River Lane crossing

Dear Sir or Madam,

On behalf of the school beside River Lane crossing, I write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone with signs. This is what happens at the crossing on each day of the school week.

Crossing Watch video observation lasted 6.8 minutes (408.0 s). During that time 4 pedestrian crossings and 32 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 39.7 km/h.

In that period there were 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass defined as 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. In 3 cases the pedestrian was first and in 1 case the vehicle was first.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 41.4 km/h with a separation of 0.8 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 4.0 percent, based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15 plus. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 15.5 km/h with a death risk of 0.4 percent.

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 20.6 km/h with a separation of 1.0 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.6 percent. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6 percent.

A third serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 12.9 km/h with a separation of 0.3 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3 percent. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 12.9 km/h with a death risk of 0.3 percent.

One close pass involved a car at 16.0 km/h with a separation of 2.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0 percent.

Regarding longer-term warrants, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 6.8. The share of time inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed was 95.7 percent, from 8 gaps of 6 s or more including 2 gaps of 12 s or more with the longest gap 83.4 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. For reference, the UK Traffic Signs Manual chapter 6, 13.5.2 notes that 4 to 6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups such as children may need 10 to 12 s or longer.

We request the raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone as a physical fix to lower speeds and create safe gaps. We are willing to share the full video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table outside our school.

Of the 16 crossings, 4 of 16 crossings (1 in 4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 1 of 16 (1 in 16) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 7.3-52.4% and 0.2-30.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson). The worst events were recorded as follows. The serious event had a post-encroachment time of 1.4 s with a bus at 59.9 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 18.2% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.0 km/h impact and 0.0% death risk at a 20 km/h limit. A close pass had a gap of 1.7 s with a car at 44.6 km/h, with an adult death risk of 3.3% if hit. A second close pass had a gap of 2.1 s with a motorcycle at 40.9 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.7% if hit. A third close pass had a gap of 2.9 s with a motorcycle at 55.5 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.0% if hit.

For engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 29 pedestrians and 33 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 32.6 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can overcount. Also, 49.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps, 10 of them 12 s or more, longest 84.9 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install the raised zebra crossing with speed table identified above to reduce vehicle speeds at the crossing point. We are willing to share the video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority,

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school at River Lane crossing

We write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table outside our school.

Crossing Watch recorded 32.6 minutes (1956.0 s) at this crossing. In that time there were 16 crossings and 18 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 62.0 km/h. These figures come from a single recording and may differ on other days. Of the 16 crossings, 4 of 16 crossings (1 in 4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 1 of 16 (1 in 16) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 7.3-52.4% and 0.2-30.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 1 serious near-misses and 3 close passes, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1.5-3.0 s apart.

The worst events were recorded as follows. The serious event had a post-encroachment time of 1.4 s with a bus at 59.9 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 18.2% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.0 km/h impact and 0.0% death risk at a 20 km/h limit. A close pass had a gap of 1.7 s with a car at 44.6 km/h, with an adult death risk of 3.3% if hit. A second close pass had a gap of 2.1 s with a motorcycle at 40.9 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.7% if hit. A third close pass had a gap of 2.9 s with a motorcycle at 55.5 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.0% if hit.

For engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 29 pedestrians and 33 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 32.6 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can overcount. Also, 49.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps, 10 of them 12 s or more, longest 84.9 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install the raised zebra crossing with speed table identified above to reduce vehicle speeds at the crossing point. We are willing to share the video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements to support your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

A second serious near-miss had a PET of 1.2 s with an auto-rickshaw at 18.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5%.

One close pass had a PET of 1.8 s with a car at 57.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 8.1%.
One close pass had a PET of 2.8 s with a car at 50.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0%.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone with signs at Brook Street crossing.

We are willing to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

The most severe serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.0 s with a van at 54.0 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 11.5%, based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by a car front. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 0.0 km/h with death risk 0.0%.

A third serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with a van at 50.6 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 8.7%. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with death risk 0.6%.

A fourth serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.0 s with an auto-rickshaw at 28.1 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 1.2%. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with death risk 0.6%.

We request you provide a raised zebra crossing with speed table at Garden Road crossing to reduce speeds and give pedestrians priority.

Yours faithfully,

Yours faithfully,

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the River Lane crossing outside our school. Crossing Watch measurements over 44.8 minutes recorded 12 crossings and 13 vehicles with an 85th percentile speed of 44.3 km/h. Many of these drivers were not watching the road at all. There was 1 serious near-miss and 2 close passes, defined as a pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart for serious and 1.5 s to 3.0 s for a close pass.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.1 s with a motorcycle at 36.1 km/h, carrying an adult death risk of 2.5% if hit by a car front per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

Another close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.5 s with a car at 37.3 km/h, carrying an adult death risk of 2.8% if hit by a car front per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for those crossing.

We can share the video and measurement files on request and would welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvements at Cedar Lane crossing

We write concerning the crossing outside our school at Cedar Lane crossing. A video survey of 43.5 minutes (2610.0 s) recorded 22 crossings and 15 vehicles.

In that period, 3 of 22 crossings (1 in 7.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 2 of 22 (1 in 11) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 2.9-34.9% and 1.1-29.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The 85th percentile speed was 51.2 km/h. This change is certain to save lives at this crossing. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and close pass as 1.5-3.0 s. There were 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.4 s and involved an auto-rickshaw at 49.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 8.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

A second serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s and involved a bus at 12.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s and involved a car at 25.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, based on 30 pedestrians and 21 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 43.5 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can double-count.

Also, 49.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 gaps, 4 of them 12 s or more, and the longest 84.8 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request to make the crossing outside the school safer

We are writing about the crossing on Orchard Lane outside our school. A 4.0 minute (240.0 s) video recording made by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time measured 10 pedestrian crossings and 23 moving vehicles.

The headline result was that 3 of 10 crossings (1 in 3.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 1 of 10 (1 in 10) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 6.7-65.2% and 0.3-44.5% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The 85th-percentile speed of moving vehicles was 50.5 km/h. The people crossing in these events were our students. Using the standard definitions where serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass means 1.5-3.0 s apart, there was 1 serious near-miss and 2 close passes.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s with a car travelling at 32.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed, Rosén & Sander 2009 estimates a death risk of 1.8%. 
A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.4 s with a car travelling at 44.3 km/h. 
Another close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.5 s with an auto-rickshaw travelling at 37.3 km/h.

For engineering context we note only that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 4.0 minutes, so that calculation cannot be used here. Also 81.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps, 11 of them 12 s or more, longest 22.8 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide protected priority for school children and other pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review and to discuss the site further.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request to make the crossing outside the school safer

We are writing about the crossing on Orchard Lane outside our school. A 4.0 minute (240.0 s) video recording made by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time measured 10 pedestrian crossings and 23 moving vehicles.

The headline result was that 3 of 10 crossings (1 in 3.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 1 of 10 (1 in 10) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 6.7-65.2% and 0.3-44.5% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The 85th-percentile speed of moving vehicles was 50.5 km/h. In the near-miss with a time gap of 1.2 s the vehicle was going at 32.3 km/h, and in the one with a time gap of 2.4 s it was going at 44.3 km/h. Using the standard definitions where serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass means 1.5-3.0 s apart, there was 1 serious near-miss and 2 close passes.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s with a car travelling at 32.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed, Rosén & Sander 2009 estimates a death risk of 1.8%. 
A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.4 s with a car travelling at 44.3 km/h. 
Another close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.5 s with an auto-rickshaw travelling at 37.3 km/h.

For engineering context we note only that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 4.0 minutes, so that calculation cannot be used here. Also 81.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps, 11 of them 12 s or more, longest 22.8 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide protected priority for school children and other pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review and to discuss the site further.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvements at Cedar Lane crossing

We write concerning the crossing outside our school at Cedar Lane crossing. A video survey of 43.5 minutes (2610.0 s) recorded 22 crossings and 15 vehicles.

In that period, 3 of 22 crossings (1 in 7.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 2 of 22 (1 in 11) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 2.9-34.9% and 1.1-29.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The 85th percentile speed was 51.2 km/h. Many of these drivers were not watching the road at all. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and close pass as 1.5-3.0 s. There were 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.4 s and involved an auto-rickshaw at 49.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 8.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

A second serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s and involved a bus at 12.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s and involved a car at 25.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, based on 30 pedestrians and 21 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 43.5 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can double-count.

Also, 49.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 gaps, 4 of them 12 s or more, and the longest 84.8 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Garden Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school asked for a video review of Garden Road crossing. Measurements were made by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time over 18.1 minutes, which is 1086.0 s, during which 11 crossings and 26 vehicles were observed.

In that recording, 4 of 11 crossings (1 in 2.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 4 of 11 (1 in 2.8) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 10.9-69.2% and 10.9-69.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). The 85th percentile speed was 59.2 km/h. There have already been injuries at this spot this school year. Of the 4 serious near-misses, defined as less than 1.5 s apart, 1 was person-first, 2 were vehicle-first and 1 was both at once.

The most severe serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.0 s with a van at 54.0 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 11.5%, based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by a car front. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 0.0 km/h with death risk 0.0%.

A second serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.5 s with a car at 52.1 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 9.9%. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with death risk 0.6%.

A third serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with a van at 50.6 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 8.7%. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with death risk 0.6%.

A fourth serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.0 s with an auto-rickshaw at 28.1 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 1.2%. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with death risk 0.6%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, scaled from 18.1 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count one twice. In the video, 50.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 gap of 6 s or more and 1 of 12 s or more and longest gap 67.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you provide a raised zebra crossing with speed table at Garden Road crossing to reduce speeds and give pedestrians priority.

We are willing to share the video and measurement files for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at River Lane crossing

Dear Sir or Madam,

On behalf of the school beside River Lane crossing, I write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone with signs.

Crossing Watch video observation lasted 6.8 minutes (408.0 s). During that time 4 pedestrian crossings and 32 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 39.7 km/h. Most of the 32 vehicles were speeding above the posted limit during the morning peak.

In that period there were 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass defined as 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. In 3 cases the pedestrian was first and in 1 case the vehicle was first.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 41.4 km/h with a separation of 0.8 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 4.0 percent, based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15 plus. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 15.5 km/h with a death risk of 0.4 percent.

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 20.6 km/h with a separation of 1.0 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.6 percent. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6 percent.

A third serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 12.9 km/h with a separation of 0.3 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3 percent. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 12.9 km/h with a death risk of 0.3 percent.

One close pass involved a car at 16.0 km/h with a separation of 2.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0 percent.

Regarding longer-term warrants, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 6.8. The share of time inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed was 95.7 percent, from 8 gaps of 6 s or more including 2 gaps of 12 s or more with the longest gap 83.4 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. For reference, the UK Traffic Signs Manual chapter 6, 13.5.2 notes that 4 to 6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups such as children may need 10 to 12 s or longer.

We request the raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone as a physical fix to lower speeds and create safe gaps. We are willing to share the full video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Garden Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school asked for a video review of Garden Road crossing. Measurements were made by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time over 18.1 minutes, which is 1086.0 s, during which 11 crossings and 26 vehicles were observed.

In that recording, 4 of 11 crossings (1 in 2.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 4 of 11 (1 in 2.8) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 10.9-69.2% and 10.9-69.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). The 85th percentile speed was 59.2 km/h. The recording these figures come from lasted 18.1 minutes. Of the 4 serious near-misses, defined as less than 1.5 s apart, 1 was person-first, 2 were vehicle-first and 1 was both at once.

The most severe serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.0 s with a van at 54.0 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 11.5%, based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by a car front. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 0.0 km/h with death risk 0.0%.

A second serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.5 s with a car at 52.1 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 9.9%. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with death risk 0.6%.

A third serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with a van at 50.6 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 8.7%. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with death risk 0.6%.

A fourth serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.0 s with an auto-rickshaw at 28.1 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 1.2%. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with death risk 0.6%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, scaled from 18.1 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count one twice. In the video, 50.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 gap of 6 s or more and 1 of 12 s or more and longest gap 67.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you provide a raised zebra crossing with speed table at Garden Road crossing to reduce speeds and give pedestrians priority.

We are willing to share the video and measurement files for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by The Principal as head of the school

Dear Road Authority,

At the Market Street crossing, 28.2 minutes of video recorded 14 crossings and 1 moving vehicle, with 85th percentile speed of 30.0 km/h. To sum up, the recording showed 1 serious near-miss and 0 close passes.

The serious near-miss involved a car and a person on the same spot 0.8 s apart. The car speed was 28.9 km/h. For adults hit by a car front, the death risk at that speed is 1.3% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts. At a 20.0 km/h limit the impact would be 20.0 km/h with death risk of 0.6% for adults hit by a car front.

PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 30 pedestrians and 2 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 28.2 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count 1.3x the true count. 62.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 gap, with 1 of them 12 s or more, longest 28.9 s, with the caveat that edge gaps are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing at this location. We offer to share the video for review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Brook Street crossing

I write as head of the school beside Brook Street crossing. A video survey by Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measured 7 pedestrian crossings and 34 moving vehicles in 4.9 minutes (294.0 s).

The 85th percentile speed was 59.4 km/h. All of the pedestrians involved were children on their way home. Regarding gaps, 43.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 11 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 58.4 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video. PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this recording is 4.9 minutes, so those rates are not reported.

We recorded 3 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s). Arrival order was 1 person first, 3 vehicle first and 1 both at once.

The worst cases were:
One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.0 s with an auto-rickshaw at 17.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.
A second serious near-miss had a PET of 1.2 s with an auto-rickshaw at 18.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5%.
A third serious near-miss had a PET of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 13.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.
One close pass had a PET of 1.8 s with a car at 57.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 8.1%.
One close pass had a PET of 2.8 s with a car at 50.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0%.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone with signs at Brook Street crossing.

We are willing to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about safety at the Station Road crossing outside our school.

In 9.3 minutes of video (558.0 s) we recorded 3 pedestrian crossings and 19 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 31.9 km/h. Parents see the same danger here at each school dismissal. 3 of 3 crossings (1 in 1) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s, and 2 of 3 (1 in 1.5) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 29.2-100.0% and 9.4-99.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

There were 2 serious near-misses (less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 close pass (1.5-3.0 s). One serious near-miss had a car at 34.3 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.0 s. The modelled adult death risk if hit by the car front for that impact is 2.2%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). A second serious near-miss had a van at 30.8 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s. The modelled adult death risk if hit by the car front for that impact is 1.6%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h. A close pass had a car at 14.6 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.6 s.

PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 9.3, with 3 pedestrian crossings and 19 moving vehicles counted. 50.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 81.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and protect pupils.

We are happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the School Lane crossing on behalf of the school. A video of 7.8 minutes (468.0 s) was analysed by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time. In that period there were 6 pedestrian crossings and 23 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 54.5 km/h. In the near-miss with a time gap of 0.0 s the vehicle was going at 37.4 km/h, and in the one with a time gap of 0.8 s it was going at 17.8 km/h.

For context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 7.8 minutes. In the video 86.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed. There were 10 gaps of 6 s or more, 2 of them 12 s or more, with the longest gap 21.1 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

The analysis found 2 serious near-misses and 3 close passes. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. Close pass is 1.5 to 3.0 s.

One serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.0 s with a bus at 37.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk at that speed is 2.8%. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 20.0 km/h with an adult death risk of 0.6%.

A second serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.8 s with a bus at 17.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk at that speed is 0.5%. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 17.8 km/h with an adult death risk of 0.5%. Risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

A close pass had a time gap of 2.1 s with an auto-rickshaw at 54.7 km/h.

A close pass had a time gap of 2.7 s with a car at 19.6 km/h.

A close pass had a time gap of 2.9 s with a car at 14.5 km/h.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for children and other pedestrians crossing to school.

We are happy to share the video and the full measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Road Authority,

At the Market Street crossing, 28.2 minutes of video recorded 14 crossings and 1 moving vehicle, with 85th percentile speed of 30.0 km/h. This is what happens at the crossing on each day of the school week.

The serious near-miss involved a car and a person on the same spot 0.8 s apart. The car speed was 28.9 km/h. For adults hit by a car front, the death risk at that speed is 1.3% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts. At a 20.0 km/h limit the impact would be 20.0 km/h with death risk of 0.6% for adults hit by a car front.

PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 30 pedestrians and 2 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 28.2 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count 1.3x the true count. 62.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 gap, with 1 of them 12 s or more, longest 28.9 s, with the caveat that edge gaps are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing at this location. We offer to share the video for review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority,

We write concerning the crossing outside our school at Brook Street crossing.

We arranged video monitoring using SAM tracking with road-plane geometry. In 17.4 minutes we recorded 20 pedestrian crossings and 24 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 44.9 km/h. Several children have been hurt at this crossing since the term began. There were 2 serious near-misses where pedestrian and moving vehicle were on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 4 close passes between 1.5 s and 3.0 s.

The most severe event had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s and involved a motorcycle. That motorcycle was travelling at 37.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 2.8%.

A second serious event had a post-encroachment time of 0.5 s and involved a car. That car was travelling at 17.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 0.5%.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.6 s and involved a bus. That bus was travelling at 22.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 0.6%.

A further close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.8 s and involved a motorcycle. That motorcycle was travelling at 22.8 km/h.

A final close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.5 s and involved a bus. That bus was travelling at 30.8 km/h. All risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009.

Engineering review noted PV² of 0.0 x 10^8 based on 69 pedestrians and 83 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 17.4 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can double-count. It also noted 56.4% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 5 such gaps and longest 11.1 s, though the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a speed table to reduce speeds and provide protected crossing time.

We are happy to share the video and underlying measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvements at Cedar Lane crossing

We write concerning the crossing outside our school at Cedar Lane crossing. A video survey of 43.5 minutes (2610.0 s) recorded 22 crossings and 15 vehicles.

In that period, 3 of 22 crossings (1 in 7.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 2 of 22 (1 in 11) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 2.9-34.9% and 1.1-29.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The 85th percentile speed was 51.2 km/h. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and close pass as 1.5-3.0 s. There were 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass. Across the 22 crossings, 1 had the person arrive first, 2 had the vehicle arrive first, and 0 had both arrive at the same time.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.4 s and involved an auto-rickshaw at 49.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 8.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

A second serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s and involved a bus at 12.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s and involved a car at 25.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, based on 30 pedestrians and 21 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 43.5 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can double-count.

Also, 49.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 gaps, 4 of them 12 s or more, and the longest 84.8 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Brook Street crossing

I write as head of the school beside Brook Street crossing. A video survey by Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measured 7 pedestrian crossings and 34 moving vehicles in 4.9 minutes (294.0 s).

The 85th percentile speed was 59.4 km/h. Many drivers were clearly exceeding the posted school-zone limit as they passed the crossing. Regarding gaps, 43.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 11 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 58.4 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video. PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this recording is 4.9 minutes, so those rates are not reported.

We recorded 3 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s). Arrival order was 1 person first, 3 vehicle first and 1 both at once.

The worst cases were:
One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.0 s with an auto-rickshaw at 17.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.
A second serious near-miss had a PET of 1.2 s with an auto-rickshaw at 18.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5%.
A third serious near-miss had a PET of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 13.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.
One close pass had a PET of 1.8 s with a car at 57.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 8.1%.
One close pass had a PET of 2.8 s with a car at 50.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0%.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone with signs at Brook Street crossing.

We are willing to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the School Lane crossing on behalf of the school. A video of 7.8 minutes (468.0 s) was analysed by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time. In that period there were 6 pedestrian crossings and 23 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 54.5 km/h. Had a child been struck, the impact would almost certainly have been fatal.

For context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 7.8 minutes. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

One serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.0 s with a bus at 37.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk at that speed is 2.8%. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 20.0 km/h with an adult death risk of 0.6%.

A second serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.8 s with a bus at 17.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk at that speed is 0.5%. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 17.8 km/h with an adult death risk of 0.5%. Risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

A close pass had a time gap of 2.1 s with an auto-rickshaw at 54.7 km/h.

A close pass had a time gap of 2.7 s with a car at 19.6 km/h.

A close pass had a time gap of 2.9 s with a car at 14.5 km/h.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for children and other pedestrians crossing to school.

We are happy to share the video and the full measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Station Road crossing

The closest pass was 2.2 s apart with a van at 28.1 km/h. The 2nd closest pass was 2.8 s apart with a van at 14.5 km/h. For adults hit by a car front the modelled death risk if hit is 0.0% in each case (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We can share the full video and Crossing Watch data on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about safety at the Station Road crossing outside our school.

Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 29.2-100.0% and 9.4-99.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

There were 2 serious near-misses (less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 close pass (1.5-3.0 s). One serious near-miss had a car at 34.3 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.0 s. The modelled adult death risk if hit by the car front for that impact is 2.2%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). A second serious near-miss had a van at 30.8 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s. The modelled adult death risk if hit by the car front for that impact is 1.6%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h. A close pass had a car at 14.6 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.6 s.

PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 9.3, with 3 pedestrian crossings and 19 moving vehicles counted. During the 558.0 s of footage there were 10 gaps with no moving vehicle at the crossing that lasted 6 s or more, including 3 gaps that lasted 12 s or more. 50.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 81.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and protect pupils.

We are happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Road Authority,

For adults hit by a car front, the death risk at that speed is 1.3% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts. Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvements at Cedar Lane crossing

We write concerning the crossing outside our school at Cedar Lane crossing. A video survey of 43.5 minutes (2610.0 s) recorded 22 crossings and 15 vehicles.

In that period, three of 22 crossings (1 in 7.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 2 of 22 (1 in 11) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 2.9-34.9% and 1.1-29.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The 85th percentile speed was 51.2 km/h. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and close pass as 1.5-3.0 s. There were 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.4 s and involved an auto-rickshaw at 49.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 8.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

A second serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s and involved a bus at 12.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s and involved a car at 25.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, based on 30 pedestrians and 21 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 43.5 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can double-count.

Also, 49.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 gaps, 4 of them 12 s or more, and the longest 84.8 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority,

We write concerning the crossing outside our school at Brook Street crossing.

We arranged video monitoring using SAM tracking with road-plane geometry. In 17.4 minutes we recorded 20 pedestrian crossings and 24 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 44.9 km/h. There were two serious near-misses where pedestrian and moving vehicle were on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 4 close passes between 1.5 s and 3.0 s.

The most severe event had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s and involved a motorcycle. That motorcycle was travelling at 37.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 2.8%.

A second serious event had a post-encroachment time of 0.5 s and involved a car. That car was travelling at 17.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 0.5%.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.6 s and involved a bus. That bus was travelling at 22.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 0.6%.

A further close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.8 s and involved a motorcycle. That motorcycle was travelling at 22.8 km/h.

A final close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.5 s and involved a bus. That bus was travelling at 30.8 km/h. All risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009.

Engineering review noted PV² of 0.0 x 10^8 based on 69 pedestrians and 83 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 17.4 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can double-count. It also noted 56.4% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 5 such gaps and longest 11.1 s, though the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a speed table to reduce speeds and provide protected crossing time.

We are happy to share the video and underlying measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write regarding safety outside our school at Lake View Road crossing.

We measured traffic from video for 2.4 minutes. In that time there were 5 pedestrian crossings and 6 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 50.9 km/h.

For context on engineering assessment, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 2.4. In the period recorded, 61.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed. During the 2.4 minutes there were 9 gaps of at least 6 s, including 8 gaps of at least 12 s, with the longest gap reaching 21.4 s.

We recorded 5 serious near-misses. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart.

One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.0 s with a motorcycle travelling at 45.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 5.5%.
One serious near-miss had a PET of 1.1 s with a car travelling at 38.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 3.1%.
One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.7 s with a car travelling at 34.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.3%.
One serious near-miss had a PET of 1.4 s with a van travelling at 23.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.9%.
One serious near-miss had a PET of 1.0 s with a motorcycle travelling at 16.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4%.

Risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosen and Sander 2009.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and protect pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at River Lane crossing

Dear Sir or Madam,

On behalf of the school beside River Lane crossing, I write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone with signs. There have already been injuries at this spot this school year.

Crossing Watch video observation lasted 6.8 minutes (408.0 s). During that time 4 pedestrian crossings and 32 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 39.7 km/h.

In that period there were 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass defined as 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. In 3 cases the pedestrian was first and in 1 case the vehicle was first.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 41.4 km/h with a separation of 0.8 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 4.0 percent, based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15 plus. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 15.5 km/h with a death risk of 0.4 percent.

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 20.6 km/h with a separation of 1.0 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.6 percent. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6 percent.

A third serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 12.9 km/h with a separation of 0.3 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3 percent. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 12.9 km/h with a death risk of 0.3 percent.

One close pass involved a car at 16.0 km/h with a separation of 2.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0 percent.

Regarding longer-term warrants, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 6.8. The share of time inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed was 95.7 percent, from 8 gaps of 6 s or more including 2 gaps of 12 s or more with the longest gap 83.4 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. For reference, the UK Traffic Signs Manual chapter 6, 13.5.2 notes that 4 to 6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups such as children may need 10 to 12 s or longer.

We request the raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone as a physical fix to lower speeds and create safe gaps. We are willing to share the full video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the School Lane crossing on behalf of the school. A video of 7.8 minutes (468.0 s) was analysed by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time. In that period there were 6 pedestrian crossings and 23 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 54.5 km/h.

For context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 7.8 minutes. In the video 86.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed. There were 10 gaps of 6 s or more, 2 of them 12 s or more, with the longest gap 21.1 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

The analysis found 2 serious near-misses and 3 close passes. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. Close pass is 1.5 to 3.0 s.

One serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.0 s with a bus at 37.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk at that speed is 2.8%. If hit at these speeds, a child would have faced a 10% chance of dying. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 20.0 km/h with an adult death risk of 0.6%.

A second serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.8 s with a bus at 17.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk at that speed is 0.5%. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 17.8 km/h with an adult death risk of 0.5%. Risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

A close pass had a time gap of 2.1 s with an auto-rickshaw at 54.7 km/h.

A close pass had a time gap of 2.7 s with a car at 19.6 km/h.

A close pass had a time gap of 2.9 s with a car at 14.5 km/h.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for children and other pedestrians crossing to school.

We are happy to share the video and the full measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Ring Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

I write on behalf of the school located at the Ring Road crossing to request a safety improvement.

We commissioned a video review of the crossing. During 4.0 minutes (240.0 s) of video, 3 pedestrian crossings and 13 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 49.5 km/h.

No serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) were recorded. There were 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s apart).

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about safety at the Station Road crossing outside our school.

In 9.3 minutes of video (558.0 s) we recorded 3 pedestrian crossings and 19 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 31.9 km/h. To sum up, the recording showed 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass. 3 of 3 crossings (1 in 1) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s, and 2 of 3 (1 in 1.5) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 29.2-100.0% and 9.4-99.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

There were 2 serious near-misses (less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 close pass (1.5-3.0 s). One serious near-miss had a car at 34.3 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.0 s. The modelled adult death risk if hit by the car front for that impact is 2.2%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). A second serious near-miss had a van at 30.8 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s. The modelled adult death risk if hit by the car front for that impact is 1.6%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h. A close pass had a car at 14.6 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.6 s.

PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 9.3, with 3 pedestrian crossings and 19 moving vehicles counted. 50.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 81.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and protect pupils.

We are happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvements at Cedar Lane crossing

We write concerning the crossing outside our school at Cedar Lane crossing. A video survey of 43.5 minutes (2610.0 s) recorded 22 crossings and 15 vehicles.

In that period, 3 of 22 crossings (1 in 7.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 2 of 22 (1 in 11) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 2.9-34.9% and 1.1-29.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The 85th percentile speed was 51.2 km/h. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and close pass as 1.5-3.0 s. There were 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.4 s and involved an auto-rickshaw at 49.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 8.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

A second serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s and involved a bus at 12.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.

A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s and involved a car at 25.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, based on 30 pedestrians and 21 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 43.5 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can double-count.

Also, 49.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 gaps, 4 of them 12 s or more, and the longest 84.8 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We request a raised zebra crossing at this spot to slow vehicles to near 20.0 km/h at the conflict point.

We will share the video and tracking on request to assist design.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We are happy to share the video and measurements to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Garden Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school asked for a video review of Garden Road crossing. Measurements were made by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time over 18.1 minutes, which is 1086.0 s, during which 11 crossings and 26 vehicles were observed.

In that recording, 4 of 11 crossings (1 in 2.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 4 of 11 (1 in 2.8) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 10.9-69.2% and 10.9-69.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). The 85th percentile speed was 59.2 km/h. In the near-miss with a time gap of 1.0 s the vehicle was going at 52.1 km/h, and in the one with a time gap of 0.5 s it was going at 54.0 km/h. Of the 4 serious near-misses, defined as less than 1.5 s apart, 1 was person-first, 2 were vehicle-first and 1 was both at once.

The most severe serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.0 s with a van at 54.0 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 11.5%, based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by a car front. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 0.0 km/h with death risk 0.0%.

A second serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.5 s with a car at 52.1 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 9.9%. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with death risk 0.6%.

A third serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with a van at 50.6 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 8.7%. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with death risk 0.6%.

A fourth serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.0 s with an auto-rickshaw at 28.1 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 1.2%. At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 20.0 km/h with death risk 0.6%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, scaled from 18.1 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count one twice. In the video, 50.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 gap of 6 s or more and 1 of 12 s or more and longest gap 67.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you provide a raised zebra crossing with speed table at Garden Road crossing to reduce speeds and give pedestrians priority.

We are willing to share the video and measurement files for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by The Principal as head of the school
